title: Circles
description: Calculate circumference and area of circles; understand radius, diameter and pi.

notes.heading: Parts of a Circle

illustration.alt: Diagram of a circle showing the centre, radius, diameter and circumference.
illustration.caption: The radius is half the diameter; the circumference is the distance around the circle.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
A circle is a shape where every point on the curve is the same distance from the centre.

🔑 Key Concepts
• The centre is the fixed middle point.
• The radius ($r$) is the distance from the centre to any point on the circle.
• The diameter ($d$) is a straight line passing through the centre and touching the circle at both ends.
• The circumference ($C$) is the distance around the circle.

💡 Worked Example
In a circle with radius $5~\text{cm}$, the diameter is $d = 2r = 2 \times 5 = 10~\text{cm}$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The diameter is twice the radius: $d = 2r$.
• The radius is half the diameter: $r = \frac{d}{2}$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Mixing up the radius and diameter when reading a diagram.

notes.heading: The Number $\pi$
notes.body:
📌 Definition
$\pi$ (pi) is the number of times the diameter fits around the circumference of any circle.

🔑 Key Concept
$\pi$ is approximately $3.14159...$ It is an irrational number, so its decimal digits never end or repeat.
For calculations you can use $\pi \approx 3.14$ or the $\pi$ button on a calculator.

💡 Worked Example
Estimate the circumference of a circle with diameter $7~\text{cm}$ using $\pi \approx \frac{22}{7}$.
$$C = \pi d \approx \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = 22~\text{cm}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $\pi$ is the same for every circle, no matter how large or small.
• Using $3.14$ gives an approximate answer; the $\pi$ key gives a more accurate answer.

✅ Check
If a diameter is about $3$ units, the circumference is about $3\pi \approx 9.42$ units.

notes.heading: Circumference of a Circle
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The circumference ($C$) is the distance around a circle.

🔑 Formulas
$$C = \pi d$$
$$C = 2\pi r$$
where $d$ is the diameter and $r$ is the radius.

💡 Worked Example
Find the circumference of a circle with radius $4~\text{cm}$. Use $\pi \approx 3.14$.
$$C = 2\pi r = 2 \times 3.14 \times 4 = 25.12~\text{cm}$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using the diameter formula with the radius, or forgetting to double the radius when using $C = 2\pi r$.

✅ Check
A radius of $4~\text{cm}$ means a diameter of $8~\text{cm}$. Then $C = \pi d \approx 3.14 \times 8 = 25.12~\text{cm}$, which matches.

notes.heading: Area of a Circle
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The area ($A$) of a circle is the space inside its circumference.

🔑 Formula
$$A = \pi r^2$$
This means $\pi \times r \times r$, not $\pi \times 2r$.

💡 Worked Example
Find the area of a circle with radius $3~\text{cm}$. Use $\pi \approx 3.14$.
$$A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times 3^2 = 3.14 \times 9 = 28.26~\text{cm}^2$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Squaring the radius incorrectly: $3^2 = 9$, not $6$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Area units are square units, e.g. $\text{cm}^2$.
• If you are given the diameter, halve it first to find $r$.

notes.heading: Finding Circumference and Area from Diameter
notes.body:
📌 Definition
When a question gives the diameter, halve it to find the radius before using $A = \pi r^2$.

🔑 How it works
1. Write down the diameter $d$.
2. Find the radius: $r = \frac{d}{2}$.
3. Substitute into the formula you need.

💡 Worked Example
A circle has diameter $10~\text{cm}$. Find its area.
$$r = \frac{10}{2} = 5~\text{cm}$$
$$A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times 5^2 = 3.14 \times 25 = 78.5~\text{cm}^2$$

✅ Check
The radius is $5~\text{cm}$, so the circumference would be $C = 2\pi r \approx 31.4~\text{cm}$. That is a sensible length for a $10~\text{cm}$ diameter circle.

notes.heading: Finding the Radius from the Circumference
notes.body:
📌 Definition
If you know the circumference, you can rearrange $C = 2\pi r$ to find $r$.

🔑 How it works
$$r = \frac{C}{2\pi}$$

💡 Worked Example
A circle has circumference $31.4~\text{cm}$. Find its radius using $\pi \approx 3.14$.
$$r = \frac{31.4}{2 \times 3.14} = \frac{31.4}{6.28} = 5~\text{cm}$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Dividing by $\pi$ but forgetting to divide by $2$. The denominator is $2\pi$, not $\pi$.

✅ Check
If $r = 5~\text{cm}$, then $C = 2 \times 3.14 \times 5 = 31.4~\text{cm}$, which matches the given circumference.

notes.heading: Finding the Radius from the Area
notes.body:
📌 Definition
If you know the area, rearrange $A = \pi r^2$ to find $r$.

🔑 How it works
$$r^2 = \frac{A}{\pi}$$
$$r = \sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}}$$
Take the square root to find the radius.

💡 Worked Example
A circle has area $78.5~\text{cm}^2$. Find its radius using $\pi \approx 3.14$.
$$r^2 = \frac{78.5}{3.14} = 25$$
$$r = \sqrt{25} = 5~\text{cm}$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to take the square root. The value $25$ is $r^2$, so $r = 5$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The radius must be a positive length, so take the positive square root.

notes.heading: Circle Calculations Checklist
notes.body:
📎 Key Points to Remember
• Radius to diameter: $d = 2r$.
• Diameter to radius: $r = \frac{d}{2}$.
• Circumference: $C = \pi d = 2\pi r$.
• Area: $A = \pi r^2$.
• Always check whether the question gives the radius or the diameter.
• Use the same units throughout a calculation.

✅ Check
For a circle with radius $6~\text{cm}$:
$$C = 2 \times 3.14 \times 6 = 37.68~\text{cm}$$
$$A = 3.14 \times 6^2 = 113.04~\text{cm}^2$$

questions.stem: A circle has radius $6~\text{cm}$. What is its diameter?
questions.explanation: The diameter is twice the radius: $d = 2r = 2 \times 6 = 12~\text{cm}$.

questions.stem: A circle has diameter $14~\text{cm}$. What is its radius?
questions.explanation: The radius is half the diameter: $r = \frac{d}{2} = \frac{14}{2} = 7~\text{cm}$.

questions.stem: What is the approximate value of $\pi$?
questions.explanation: $\pi$ is approximately $3.14$; the other values are common approximations for different constants.

Which formula gives the area of a circle?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is $A = \pi r^2$. The other formulas give circumference or an incorrect area.

questions.stem: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle using the radius?
questions.explanation: $C = 2\pi r$ uses the radius. $C = \pi d$ is equivalent but uses the diameter.
